national_raw_news.title: PM Modi inaugurates and lays foundation stone Pune Metro projects worth Rs 21,800 crore
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that Pune is playing an important role in shaping the vision of a developed India and that the expansion of the metro network is accelerating the city’s development. The metro has given Pune a new identity by providing citizens with modern, efficient and high-quality public transport facilities, which are also contributing to the city’s economic growth. The Prime Minister extended Diwali greetings to the people before addressing the gathering. The Prime Minister virtually inaugurated the much-awaited Hinjawadi-Maan to Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 by flagging off a metro train. The service will be open to passengers from November 4, 2026. He also virtually performed the foundation stone-laying ceremony for four new Pune Metro Phase-II corridors: Vanaz to Chandani Chowk, Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, Kharadi to Khadakwasla and Nal Stop to Manik Baug. Governor Jishnu Dev Varma and Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Manohar Lal attended the programme virtually. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Union Minister of State for Civil Aviation and Cooperation Murlidhar Mohol, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar were present. The Prime Minister said that metro services are now operational in 26 cities across the country, with the total metro network expanding from approximately 248 kilometres to more than 1,200 kilometres. Over one crore passengers travel by metro every day. Maharashtra alone has around 175 kilometres of operational metro network. He further stated that the Central Government has undertaken extensive infrastructure development in the energy, road and railway sectors over the past twelve years to achieve the goal of a developed India. Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said that the Maharashtra Government is committed to expanding the metro network and strengthening public transport facilities through various metro projects. Around 120 kilometres of additional metro corridors will provide citizens with modern, safe and environment-friendly transportation. He added that metro projects would not only reduce travel time but also boost trade, industries, employment opportunities and economic activity. An investment of approximately Rs. 5,000 crore would give a significant boost to the urban economy. He expressed confidence that the metro would become a new engine of urban development. The Hinjawadi-Maan to Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 is 23 kilometres long and has 23 stations. In the first phase, passenger services will begin at 17 stations, while the remaining six stations will be opened in phases by January 2027. The Pune Metro project has received substantial financial investment. More than Rs. 8,300 crore has been spent on Phase I, while approximately Rs. 13,500 crore is expected to be invested in Phase II. The combined expenditure on both phases is estimated to exceed Rs. 22,000 crore. A major feature of Metro Line 3 is that the entire metro service will be operated by women train operators. In addition, 30 per cent of the energy requirement will be met through solar power. The new metro corridor is expected to provide significant relief to IT professionals working at Hinjawadi IT Park, students and daily commuters. It will help reduce traffic congestion, save travel time and strengthen public transportation in Pune. The inauguration marks an important milestone in Pune’s infrastructure development and is expected to give fresh momentum to the city’s economic growth.

national_raw_news.title: Domestic indices surge around 1.6% extending winning streak for fourth consecutive session
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices surged around 1.6 per cent today, extending their winning streak for the fourth consecutive session. The Sensex jumped 1,225 points to close at 76,918. The Nifty climbed 370 points to settle at 23,811. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 1.1 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index added 0.3 per cent. I n the Sensex pack, 25 out of 30 constituent companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Hindustan Unilever gained nearly 4.2 per cent, Bharti Airtel jumped four per cent, and HDFC Bank rose over 3.6 per cent. In contrast, PowerGrid dropped almost 2.3 per cent, SBI Bank slipped nearly 1.8 per cent, and NTPC fell almost 0.9 per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 22 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, FMCG surged 3.4 per cent, Realty advanced over 2.3 per cent, and Private Banks rose nearly 2.1 per cent. In contrast, PSU Banks dropped more than 1.3 per cent, Utilities lost almost 0.9 per cent, and Power dipped 0.8 per cent. The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,510 companies advanced, 1,895 declined, and 201 remained unchanged.

national_raw_news.title: NSE International Exchange extends trading hours to facilitate international investors 53 mins ago 9
national_raw_news.content: The NSE International Exchange (NSEIX), based in Gujarat’s GIFT City, has extended its trading hours to 23:30 hours a day, allowing international investors and trading participants to access markets across Asian, European and American time zones. The NSEIX, in a statement, said that the enhanced market timings came into effect yesterday, with trading operations starting at 3:15 AM India Standard Time (IST) and closing at 2:45 AM IST the following day. The move aims to provide investors with a longer window to trade and greater flexibility to respond to developments in international markets. Under the revised schedule, the morning trading session for NSE IFSC Nifty 50 Index Futures, popularly known as GIFT Nifty, now begins at 5:15 am IST instead of 6:30 am. GIFT Nifty is closely tracked by investors and traders as an indicator of the likely opening trend of the benchmark Nifty index. NSEIX said the initiative would strengthen GIFT City’s role as an international financial centre connecting India with global capital markets. The extended trading window is also expected to help participants manage their market exposure across different global time zones. It added that with this initiative, NSEIX has set a new global benchmark to provide a continuous market for nearly 24 hours a day, five days a week. NSEIX is an international multi-asset exchange set up on June 5, 2017. It is recognised by the International Financial Services Centres Authority. The exchange offers a range of financial products, including Indian single-stock derivatives, index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks. NSE International Exchange has said that it will continue to focus on expanding international market access and developing market infrastructure to meet the changing requirements of global participants.

national_raw_news.title: Hockey: India register 5th successive win in Asian Champions Trophy in Jalandhar 9 hours ago 126
national_raw_news.content: In Hockey, the Indian Team completed an unbeaten league-stage run at the Hero Asian Champions Trophy by hammering South Korea with 8-0 at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar, last evening. In the other two matches, China and Bangladesh drew 1-1, while Japan beat Malaysia 2-1. Akashvani Correspondent reports that Indian Men’s kept the momentum throughout the match in front of a jubilant packed house. In the first quarter, they hit 3 goals and then carried on to hit rest of the five in the remaining time. Dilpreet Singh scored twice, while six others including Captain Harmanpreet Singh hit the remaining goals. Out of the total, 3 were converted from Penalty Corners and 5 were Field Goals. With this dominated win, India finished at the top of the standings with five wins from as many matches. Today is rest day. India will face Korea again in the semi-finals as the tournament will now move to Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium at Mohali, where the semis will be played on November 4th and the medal matches on November 5th. In another semi-final, second-placed Japan will face Malaysia, who finished the league stage at the third place. Akashvani’s all FM Rainbow Channels along with the Primary Channel of Akashvani Jalandhar are broadcasting India specific matches live.

national_raw_news.title: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu makes landfall near Ongole, Andhra Pradesh 9 hours ago 304
national_raw_news.content: Cyclone Murasu over the West Central Bay of Bengal crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narasapur, close to Ongole, early this morning with wind speed of 100-110 kilometres per hour, gusting to 120 kilometres per hour. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that it lay centered over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. It is likely to continue to move North-northwestwards and weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm by noon and further into a deep depression by midnight of today. The IMD has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Andhra Pradesh and Telangana today. According to IMD, places over Chhattisgarh, Odisha, South Interior Karnataka, Coastal Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal will experience heavy rainfall today. The Met Department has forecast thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha for the day. Meanwhile, the air quality in Delhi-NCR continues to remain in the very poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s air quality index was recorded at 331 at 7 AM. The sub-committee of the Commission for Air Quality Management has imposed Graded Response Action Plan- GRAP-2 restrictions in the National Capital Region. An Air Quality Index between 0 and 50 is considered good, 51 and 100 satisfactory, 101 and 200 moderate, 201 and 300 poor, and 301 and 400 very poor. An AQI between 401 and 500 is considered severe.

He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The Prime Minister will inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3, also known as the Pink Line, built at a cost of over 8,300 crore rupees. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune's urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportati...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21,800 crore rupees today through video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The Prime Minister will inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3, also known as the Pink Line, built at a cost of over 8,300 crore rupees. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune’s urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportation solutions. Spanning approximately 23 kilometres, the Pink Line connects Maan to District Court Metro station. The corridor will provide Metro connectivity between the Hinjewadi IT hub and Shivajinagar, improving access to one of Pune’s major employment centres and facilitating the daily commute of thousands of IT professionals and other commuters. The corridor will integrate with the existing metro network, providing seamless connectivity across different parts of Pune. It will help reduce dependence on private vehicles, ease traffic congestion and vehicular emissions, and improve access to major commercial and residential areas. A notable feature of the Pink Line is its emphasis on women’s empowerment and gender-inclusive public transportation. The line will be operated entirely by women train operators, making it a first-of-its-kind initiative. The project also emphasises environmental sustainability, with approximately 30 per cent of its total electricity requirements envisaged to be met through solar power. Mr Modi will also lay the foundation stone of Phase-II of Pune Metro, to be developed at an estimated cost of around 13,500 crore rupees. Phase-II comprises Pune Metro Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A, which will substantially expand the city’s Metro network and strengthen connectivity across important residential, commercial and IT hubs. Under Phase-II, Lines 2A and 2B will span a total length of around 12.75 kilometres. Line 2A will connect Vanaz to Chandani Chowk, while Line 2B will connect Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, extending the existing east-west Metro network. Line 4, spanning around 25.52 kilometres, will connect Kharadi to Khadakwasla. Line 4A, spanning 6.12 kilometres, will connect Nal Stop to Manik Baug. The new Metro corridors will connect several important locations, including Kharadi, Magarpatta, Hadapsar, Swargate, Manik Baug, Nanded City, Pune Cantonment and Warje. The eastern extension from Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi will improve connectivity to rapidly developing residential, commercial and IT hubs in Kharadi and Wagholi. The corridors will integrate with intercity bus services and the existing Pune Metro network through interchange facilities at Swargate, Nal Stop and Kharadi Bypass, facilitating seamless connectivity across different parts of the city. These projects will strengthen Pune’s public transportation infrastructure, improve connectivity across the city and provide commuters with an efficient and integrated urban mobility network.

national_raw_news.title: Unbeaten India register fifth successive win in Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026, set up semi-final clash against Korea
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Men’s Hockey Team completed an unbeaten league-stage run at the Hero Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026 on Monday with an 8-0 win over Korea – their fifth in a row – at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar. Dilpreet Singh (8′, 40′) scored twice, while Jugraj Singh (11′), Harmanpreet Singh (15′), Shilanand Lakra (33′), Sukhjeet Singh (34′), Sanjay (36′) and Angad Bir Singh (60′) were also on target. India finished at the top of the standings with five wins from five matches and will face Korea again in the semi-finals as the tournament moves to Mohali, where the semis will be played on November 4 and the medal matches on November 5. Second-placed Japan will face Malaysia, who finished the league stage in third place, in the other semi-final. India began aggressively in front of a packed house and created an early chance through Sukhjeet, whose backhand effort in the fourth minute was saved by goalkeeper Kim Jaehyeon. Dilpreet opened the scoring in the eighth minute with a backhand finish after a move that began with an aerial pass from Jugraj. India doubled their lead through a penalty corner in the 11th minute, with Jugraj scoring after Harmanpreet’s initial effort was kept out and Vishnukant Singh set up Jugraj on the rebound. Harmanpreet added another penalty-corner goal to his tally in the 15th minute to give India a 3-0 lead at the first break. He now tops the scoring chart with nine goals. Korea showed more intent in the second quarter and earned a number of penalty corners, but the Indian defence kept them at bay. Pathak also denied Son Dain in a one-on-one situation in the 27th minute with a timely save using his outstretched foot. India had opportunities of their own, but Aditya Arjun Lalage’s shot went wide, while another penalty corner did not result in a goal after the ball was ruled to have been played with the back of the stick. India went into half-time with their three-goal advantage intact. India increased the tempo after the break and added four goals in the third quarter. Shilanand Lakra scored in the 33rd minute after a penalty-corner variation. Harmanpreet’s pass found Jugraj, whose attempt was saved by Kim, but Lakra was on hand to put away the rebound. Sukhjeet made it 5-0 a minute later, deflecting Aditya’s pass from the baseline into the net. Sanjay added another in the 36th minute, reacting quickest after Dilpreet’s attempt was saved. India’s seventh goal came in the 40th minute when Sanjay controlled Harmanpreet’s long aerial pass and struck towards goal, with Dilpreet getting a touch to send the ball past the goalkeeper. India eased the tempo in the final quarter, with Korea enjoying periods of ball-possession but struggling to create clear chances. Suraj Karkera made a save when Korea threatened, while a penalty corner in the 58th minute came to nothing. Angad Bir Singh then scored a superb solo goal in the 60th minute, winning possession in the midfield, driving towards the circle and pushing the ball underneath the advancing goalkeeper to complete the 8-0 win. Korea had another penalty corner in the closing seconds, but failed to make the most of it. Sanjay, who was named ‘Player of the Match’, said India were pleased to finish at the top of the pool. “We wanted to top the table and we did that. We are very happy. I want to request the crowd to support us the same way in Mohali,” he said. India finished with 15 points and a goal difference of +29. Japan ended second with 10 points, followed by Malaysia with nine and Korea with six points. -IANS

national_raw_news.title: “Huge honour for India,” says Rijiju as Bhutan dedicates Stupa 76 to PM Modi
national_raw_news.content: Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday expressed gratitude towards Bhutan after the King of Bhutan dedicated Stupa number 76 to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Rijiju represented India at the ceremony for raising and consecrating 108 Stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City. In an X post, he wrote, “It’s a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon’ble PM @narendramodi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens.” “Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H.E. Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan. A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutan’s rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations,” he added. According to the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Rijiju conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the King of Bhutan for the gesture of dedicating a Stupa as part of the Project. The 108 Stupas project was conceived by the King of Bhutan, who also steered its implementation. In a single day, thousands of volunteers erected 108 Stupas, each 15 metres tall and separated by 108 metres on an 11.7 kilometre stretch along the Aie (Mau) River within Gelephu Mindfulness City near the border with Assam. The project aims to showcase Gelephu Mindfulness City as a prominent centre of Vajrayana Buddhism, while simultaneously representing the values and culture of the Bhutanese people, the ministry stated. Earlier today, Rijiju called on Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu, where the two leaders held “warm and very positive” discussions aimed at strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project. “Delighted to call on H.E. Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Hon’ble Prime Minister of Bhutan, in Gelephu today. Had a warm and very positive discussion on India-Bhutan partnership, and the immense potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City for both nations. India remains a steadfast partner in Bhutan’s path of growth and prosperity,” Rijiju posted on X. The Union Minister is on a visit to Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. The two sides have maintained a healthy trend in bilateral cooperation in diverse areas including development cooperation, trade, energy, investment, connectivity and cultural connections. -(ANI)

national_raw_news.content: India committed to protecting integrity of sports: Mansukh Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA Managers’ Meeting 2026 Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India committed to protecting integrity of sports: Mansukh Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA Managers’ Meeting 2026 ANI | Updated: Nov 03, 2026 19:49 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 3 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, on Tuesday, launched the Extramural Research Grant Policy of the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) at the 10th World Association of Anti-Doping Scientists (WAADS) Quality Assurance Managers’ Meeting 2026 in New Delhi, according to a press release from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The two-day meeting that began on November 2 was organised by NDTL and brought together international stakeholders from the sports and scientific communities. Mandaviya, as the chief guest, also oversaw the launch of the NDTL Newsletter at the meet. The Union Sports Minister Outlined India’s zero tolerance policy for doping. He said, “Friends, India has zero tolerance for doping. Our responsibility is to ensure that every victory is earned through talent, discipline, and hard work. Over the last two years, under the leadership of our Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, sports has been recognised as an important pillar of nation-building,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “India’s sporting journey has entered a new phase.” Highlighting India’s commitment towards further anti-doping research and education, the Union Minister said, “Today we launched the important Extramural Research Grant Policy, which aims at promoting research and development in areas of advanced detection and prevention. This initiative will strengthen the scientific foundation of our anti-doping efforts.” With India set to host Commonwealth Games 2030 and harbouring ambitions of hosting the 2036 Olympics, education and awareness about doping play a vital role in India’s fight towards preventing it. Mandaviya said, “Our approach, therefore, combines stronger testing infrastructure with education, awareness, and prevention. As India prepares to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and with our dreams of hosting the 2036 Olympics as well, anti-doping testing, athlete education, and international cooperation are a priority for us.” “Athletes, coaches, and medical professionals must understand the implications of prohibited substances, the risks associated with supplements, and their responsibilities under anti-doping rules,” Mandaviya added. The Union Sports Minister stated that India has already taken major steps towards becoming a sporting nation, and the recent performances of its athletes at the 2026 Asian Games prove that. “Through initiatives such as Khelo India, which translates to Play India, Fit India, and the target Olympic podium scheme, we have strengthened the sporting ecosystem and created greater opportunities for our youth to excel,” said Mandaviya. “At the recently concluded Asian Games 2026, our athletes delivered one of their best performances, finishing fourth in the final medal tally. Our para-athletes have also scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026, securing a record 114 medals, our highest ever medal tally at the games,” he said. national_raw_news.content: “Self-reliance is not a retreat from the world; it positions India better for global collaborations”: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर “Self-reliance is not a retreat from the world; it positions India better for global collaborations”: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh ANI | Updated: Nov 04, 2026 00:56 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 4 (ANI): Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday said military preparedness in the 21st century is closely linked to technological and industrial capabilities, emphasising the need for indigenous production of critical equipment and technologies and the capacity to sustain them independently. Addressing the third edition of the Delhi Defence Dialogue at Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA) on November 3, he emphasised that ‘Aatmanirbharta’ must be viewed as a quest for technological sovereignty, as self-reliance means ensuring that the nation's critical defence requirements are not held hostage to external dependencies. True self-reliance is achieved by possessing the knowledge to design a defence platform, the technology to manufacture it, intellectual property to improve it and the capability to sustain it throughout its lifecycle, he said. Sharing his insights on the theme of this year's Dialogue, ‘Defence Reforms, Aatmanirbharta, Collaborations and Exports’, the Defence Minister described the four elements as interconnected dimensions of India's objective to become Viksit Bharat by 2047. He stated that reforms must create an enabling institutional environment, Aatmanirbharta must strengthen indigenous technological capabilities, collaborations must accelerate access to advanced technologies and facilitate co-development, and exports must provide the scale, competitiveness and global partnerships required for a sustainable industrial ecosystem. These four elements are mutually reinforcing pillars of India's quest for strategic autonomy, he said. Rajnath Singh underlined that reforms represent the nation's willingness to change, Aatmanirbharta symbolises its determination to create, collaborations reflect its confidence to partner with the world, and exports demonstrate its readiness to compete globally. He emphasised that these four elements must progress together, as self-reliance without reforms, international collaborations and exports would limit India's technological horizons, industrial scale and global competitiveness. The Defence Minister pointed out that recent conflicts across the world have demonstrated a fundamental transformation in the character of warfare, with battlefields extending beyond land, sea and air into space, cyberspace and the digital domain. He stated that the distinction between conventional and unconventional warfare is increasingly blurring, while relatively inexpensive drones and autonomous systems are challenging sophisticated and costly military platforms. The ability to innovate rapidly, manufacture at scale and replenish capabilities has become as important as possessing advanced weapon systems, he added. Highlighting that technological and manufacturing capabilities require an enabling institutional environment, progressive policies and responsive processes, Rajnath Singh outlined the initiatives undertaken over the last decade to strengthen India's domestic defence industrial base. These include the establishment of Defence Industrial Corridors and the corporatisation of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board into seven Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), aimed at enhancing autonomy, efficiency and competitiveness in defence manufacturing.
